problem: Consider the curve ${x}^{2}+{e}^{y}=5.$ Given that $x=x(t),$   $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1$ on the curve at the point where $x=-2,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}-8\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}-8\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{e}^{x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8{e}^{x})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(8\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2y-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 8{e}^{x}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{8}{y} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6$ and $y=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-48{e}^{x}-8\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ -6\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-48{e}^{x} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $x,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $y=1$ into the equation of the curve.

At the point where $y=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-8{e}^{x}-8\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =0 \\ {1}^{2}-8{e}^{x}-8\operatorname{ln}⁡(1) & =0 \\ 1-8{e}^{x}-0 & =0 \\ -8{e}^{x} & =-1 \\ {e}^{x} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8}),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-6\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-48{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{8})} & =0 \\ -6\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =48\cdot \frac{1}{8} \\ -6\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =6 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{6}{-6} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
